Hi, I'm Chelsea Carter

I work with clients who often feel stuck and unfilled in their personal lives and intimate relationships. I support people who feel like something is missing - a situation or experience that would provide excitement, relief, comfort, or joy. I also see people who feel overwhelmed and burdened by responsibilities.

You don't have to do this alone

Healing occurs when we are joined in our experience.

Feeling fatigued and unsatisfied can be hard, especially when we feel alone. I believe healing occurs when we are joined in our experience.

I provide clients with a safe, supportive environment where they can share how they feel.

About

Chelsea Carter, LMFT

I love feeling warm.

You can find me lying under the sun, sitting by the fire, sipping tea, and soaking in warm bodies of water.

Warmth feels special to me because it soothes and relaxes my body.

When I feel warm, I feel present, happy, satisfied, and ready to connect with myself and other people.

I also love to snorkel (which, unfortunately, can be a very cold activity)!

My approach →

Approach

At the core of my work is trust.

I aim to build a strong, safe therapeutic relationship with my clients.

I attune to my clients, create space for their experience, and provide them with unconditional support and acceptance.

I acknowledge that it takes time to build trust. I create space for my clients’ past, and I seek to understand how my clients’ attachment history and lived experiences shape their current relationships.

I provide trauma informed, attachment based therapy.

I use Emotionally Focused Therapy, Internal Family Systems Therapy, somatic exercises, and drawing exercises to guide my work.

  • Emotionally Focused Therapy
  • Internal Family Systems
  • Somatic exercises
  • Drawing exercises

Common Experiences

When we feel stuck and unfilled in our personal lives and intimate relationships, it is normal to experience:

  • irritation and frustration
  • anxiety, stress, fear
  • difficulty stopping or controlling worry, difficulty falling or staying asleep
  • fatigue, burnout
  • helplessness, hopelessness
  • depression
  • low self-esteem and critical thoughts
